Root cause isolated via operator-supplied Railway build logs: Railway's Dockerfile build-LAYER cache reused a stale `vite build` (the `COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist` step logged as 'cached'; identical/partial image reuse). Service-variable workarounds were INEFFECTIVE: static ARG CACHEBUST (#61) ignored, and NO_CACHE=1 applies to Railpack not Dockerfile builds (it produced a new image but the dist layer stayed cached). Fix PR #62 squash-merged d37ba10: (1) pinned base image node:22-alpine -> node:22-alpine3.21 on all stages to break the cached layer chain and force a full rebuild incl. vite build; (2) replaced static CACHEBUST with RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA so the build cache key changes every commit automatically; (3) added /api/version (commit + build time baked into dist/version.json at build) for one-request deploy verification (/api/health left byte-identical, T-S4-7 green). CI-green. Deploy landed clean in ~45s; /api/version confirmed d37ba10 live.

The persistent 'stale frontend' signal was largely a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT: the client code-splits by route, so the native-card code lives in the lazily-loaded DocumentDetail-*.js chunk, NOT in the entry index-*.js bundle that was being grepped (both in-browser and via curl). The deployed chunk contained the markers. The genuine defect, found via live tRPC inspection (reviewSession.get): the render path is fully wired (nativeCards attached, render code deployed) but extractEmbeddedFeedbackCards returned 0 cards (nativeCardsLen:0) because reviewers (observed: Gemini) emit audience_affected as a STRING while the lenient FeedbackCardDisplaySchema typed it as z.array(z.string()) -> safeParse fails on that one field -> the WHOLE card is dropped -> silent fallback to the legacy raw body.

Fix PR #63 squash-merged 5ad3be7: FeedbackCardDisplaySchema.audience_affected now z.union([z.array(z.string()), z.string().transform(s=>[s])]).optional() (display-only projection; the strict canonical FeedbackCardSchema array contract is unchanged). Regression test added using the exact production card shape. CI-green. Deployed clean via the new per-commit cache-bust pipeline (~45s); /api/version confirmed 5ad3be7 live.

Native-card render VERIFIED LIVE on production 5ad3be7 by Claude driving Chrome as kelly (UNIVERSALTITLE browser), synthetic 'POA iteration test' doc. The same previously-failing Gemini iteration-7 session now both PARSES (tRPC reviewSession.get: all 3 suggestions nativeCardsLen:1; audience_affected coerced string->array) and RENDERS: severity-subtype chip (SUBSTANTIVE - BUSINESS), critique_type chip (structural), 'Attorney decision required' amber badge, audience line, 'Suggested revision:' formatted content (3 cards). No data mutation needed (existing data rendered post-fix). Closes MR-CAL-4C-LIVE and the MR-CAL-4B deferred render. CARRYFORWARD: AUTH_BYPASS_ENABLED still ON in prod (operator to disable); synthetic data persists (LLN-PROD-CLEANUP-1).

Evaluator / multi-reviewer topology investigation accepted/completed. Findings: the evaluator is already scaffolded (feedback_evaluations table + dispositions JSON, insertFeedbackEvaluation/getEvaluationForIteration, EVALUATOR_MODEL=anthropic:claude-opus-4-5 per decision #41, an invocation block in reviewSession.create, and ReviewPane disposition/synthesis UI) but is DORMANT and INCOMPLETE, and was disabled on purpose. Two independent reasons it does not work: (1) the evaluator block is guarded by selectedReviewers.length > 1, but the MR-0G single-reviewer gate (.max(1) + UI radio) makes that never true; (2) even if it fired, the commit path only emits telemetry - it never parses evaluator output or calls insertFeedbackEvaluation, and prompts are placeholder-level. Standing it up depends on first repairing the MR-0G-gated multi-reviewer path (MR-0 D1-D5 defects) - the largest, riskiest part - so MR-CAL-5B (multi-reviewer session data model) is the true prerequisite. Recommended (NONE authorized; each needs operator approve scope:<id>): 5B multi-reviewer data model, 5C evaluator output contract (advisory-only, consume native cards), 5D-LIVE. PRODUCT-DIRECTION NOTE: activating evaluator/multi-reviewer synthesis is a product decision (current design makes the attorney the cross-iteration synthesizer; automated synthesis is optional), not just engineering. Report: docs/engagements/MR-CAL-5A-investigation.md.

Operator product-direction decision (DESIGN ONLY; NOT scope authorization). Multi-reviewer + advisory evaluator will be TOGGLEABLE via a single GLOBAL on/off master flag, default OFF (= today's single-reviewer, attorney-as-synthesizer behavior; zero regression when off). When ON, the attorney may select multiple reviewers per review and the advisory evaluator engages (advisory only; never decision-making; attorney stays the final decision maker). Architecture must keep per-matter granularity (Option 2) addable later without rework. The toggle gates EXPOSURE only - it does NOT substitute for the MR-CAL-5B data-model repair. Build remains gated on operator approve scope:MR-CAL-5B and should BEGIN WITH A PHASE-A PLAN that re-derives the MR-0 D1-D5 defects (why multi-reviewer was disabled) and designs the flag + repaired data model for operator review before any code.
